Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.

Very important pro tip when ordering food from the canteen on the ground floor of this hospital:

If you have permission to eat on the upper floors where medical tests are conducted, because your family member cannot come down to the ground floor, do not tell any canteen staff that you are taking the food upstairs. Also, if you order a large amount of food, act as if your family member is sitting somewhere on the ground floor.

The reason is that the person who hands out food trays may refuse to give you a tray. In my experience, he created unnecessary problems for me.

After ordering more than ₹500 worth of food, he insisted that I eat the patties first and then the pizza and pasta later. I told him to give me everything at once. I also honestly informed him that my brother was upstairs as a patient undergoing tests and that we had permission to eat there.

I assumed he was trying to help, but after making me wait 20–30 minutes, when it was finally time to collect my order, he told me that trays were not allowed on the upper floors. He could have told me this before taking the order, but he didn't. It felt as though he waited until the food was ready because he thought I might cancel the order otherwise.

What's the point of allowing food to be taken upstairs if trays are not allowed? It seemed like an unnecessary rule that only created problems.

I eventually took the food upstairs without a tray. It was difficult because the plates were much smaller. My brother, who could barely walk properly, and I tried our best not to drop any food on the floor. However, crumbs from the patties and corn from the pizza still fell because the plates were too small for carrying so much food.

Hinduja Hospital, we visited your hospital for tests for my brother that cost around ₹10,000. Everyone on the upper floors—including the doctors, nurses, and reception staff—was professional, friendly, and helpful.

However, I am giving this review 1 star.

I am 29 years old, and this is the first time in my life that I have given anyone a 1-star review. Unfortunately, your canteen employee on the ground floor—the person handling payments, food distribution, and trays—left such a poor impression that it overshadowed an otherwise positive experience.

This incident happened in June 2025. I am writing this review a year later because I still remember how I was treated and how frustrating the experience was.

I experienced extremely bad treatment at Somaiya Ayurvihar Hospital, which is a trust hospital. Honestly, even government hospitals have much better behavior compared to this.
After collecting the case paper, we went to the ward for the check-up. The nurse asked us to fill out a form, but her behavior was extremely rude. She said, “Don’t fill the form here, go outside and fill it,” and also told us, “Don’t sit here, go outside.” The tone and attitude were completely disrespectful.
Then we were told that boys/male attendants are not allowed, and I was asked to wait outside during my wife’s consultation time. How can this be acceptable? If some tests or examinations are being done, it is understandable. But during consultation, at least one family member should be allowed to stay with the patient. Whatever discussion, advice, precautions, or issues are being explained by the doctor should be known to both the patient and the family member. It is not possible to explain everything properly to the patient alone.
After this, my wife met the doctor, who was also very arrogant and rude. When my wife showed her the reports, the doctor said, “These are old reports, bring new ones.” My wife politely asked the doctor to please check the date, as they were the latest reports. After checking, the doctor had no answer and went silent.
Is this really the level of professionalism expected from doctors at such a reputed hospital?
This entire experience was extremely disappointing. A hospital of this level should focus on basic respect, patient dignity, and proper communication. The staff and doctors seriously need training in behavior and patient handling.

featured_reviews.name: Sabra Murzello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently underwent a laparoscopic hysterectomy at the Namaha hospital, and I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude for the exceptional care and support I received throughout my stay.

From the very beginning, the doctors were incredibly professional, reassuring, and attentive. They took the time to explain every step of the procedure, which gave me a lot of confidence and peace of mind during a stressful time.

The dieticians also deserve a special mention for planning well-balanced, nutritious meals that supported my recovery. The food provided was not only healthy but also fresh, hygienic, and surprisingly good in taste—something that truly made a difference during my stay.

The nursing staff alol of them but special mention of Princy and housekeeping team were equally wonderful—always prompt, kind, and attentive to every need. The cleanliness and hygiene standards were consistently maintained at a very high level, which made my recovery more comfortable.

A special mention to the TPA desk(Dipti specifically always available to help on call or watsapp) as well, for handling all the insurance processes smoothly and efficiently. Their guidance and support made the entire paperwork and approval process hassle-free.

Overall, my experience was extremely positive, and I truly appreciate the dedication and compassion shown by every member of the team. Thank you for making my recovery journey so much easier.

featured_reviews.name: Smita Rathod
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently underwent a hysterectomy at Shri Namah Healthcare under the treatment of Dr. Munjal Kapadia, and my experience has been excellent. The surgery was handled very smoothly, with no pain or complications, and I did not face any issues related to anesthesia. The hospital provided outstanding services, including a well-curated inhouse diet , attentive nursing staff, and very good housekeeping. I was able to start walking on the second day after surgery, which really boosted my confidence and recovery. With proper guidance from the doctors on post-operative care, my healing process was fast and comfortable. I was able to resume my job from home within 15 days, manage all household work by 4 weeks, and even start traveling to the office by cab. The doctors and staff were extremely patient, supportive, and always ready to answer my questions. Although the diagnostic services here are on the costlier side, I was able to manage them through my company health insurance; otherwise, it may feel expensive. However, if you choose the general ward or twin sharing package or can afford the higher medical expenses, this hospital is truly one of the best choices. I highly recommend Shri Namah Healthcare with a 5-star rating for its 5-star treatment and services. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Aakanksha Joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
The care given is really good.
My mother was admitted here. They give personalized attention and good care.
The doctors are well experienced, attentive and explain you everything properly.
The staff is very helpful when it comes to solving any problem.
You are not allowed to get your food. So, if you are a patient's relative, as a local guide I would suggest don't fall for canteen food. The canteen food mostly offers biscuits and stuff like misal pav vada. 1-2 protein bars which are processed.

There is a seperate menu from which you can order food which offers options like Khichadi and dahi which are decent.
Because, when your relatives is admitted in the hospital neglecting your own health and falling for sugary oily food may not be a good option.

I would suggest they have seperate menu, which you will need to call a number and ask for, there you get better options than the processed food.

There is personalised dietician assigned to each patient. She mostly gives balanced options for the patients. I had seen Marie Biscuit in my mom's diet. I personally don't want my mom to eat biscuits with palm oil in it. So, she switched the snack.
So, if you have special preferences. You can always communicate.

One more suggestion to the hospital.
If you have a room patient's relative mostly gets assigned bed.
But if the patient is in the ICU there is no assigned bed for the patient's relative. Which is mostly offered in some other hospitals. So, that could be added.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My heartfelt gratitude to Dr. Shardul Lokare, Dr. Shantanu Lokhare, the entire team at Dhanashri Hospital, all the RMO doctors, nurses, General Duty Assistants, and every staff member who cared for my mother during her treatment and surgery.

I would like to sincerely thank Dr. Shantanu Lokhare. His thorough evaluation, medical expertise, calm approach, and attention to detail gave us great confidence before the surgery. He is not only an excellent Physician and Diabetologist but also a doctor who genuinely cares about his patients. What I appreciated most was the time he took to listen to our concerns, review every report carefully, and explain everything patiently and clearly. His guidance and support were invaluable throughout the process.

My deepest gratitude goes to Dr. Shardul Lokare, an exceptional surgeon and an outstanding human being. From the very beginning, he explained everything clearly, treated us with compassion, and performed my mother's surgery with remarkable skill and confidence. His dedication, professionalism, and commitment to patient care are truly commendable. During one of the most challenging periods for our family, his reassuring presence gave us hope and confidence.

The nursing staff, RMO doctors, and General Duty Assistants at Dhanashri Hospital deserve special appreciation. They cared for my mother day and night with patience, kindness, and professionalism. During difficult moments, their reassuring words, prompt assistance, and constant attention meant a lot to our family. Their hard work often goes unnoticed, but they play a vital role in a patient's recovery and comfort.

Today, I am happy to share that my mother is recovering well and doing much better. We firmly believe that this recovery has been possible because of the blessings, care, expertise, and teamwork of the entire medical team at Dhanashri Hospital.

I would also like to appreciate the hospital food services. The meals provided were simple, hygienic, fresh, nutritious, and perfectly suited for patients recovering from surgery. Families often worry about food during hospitalization, but the hospital's meals were thoughtfully prepared and exactly what a recovering patient needs. I would highly recommend opting for the hospital food service, as it provides healthy and balanced meals that support recovery.

Dhanashri Hospital is a place where patients are treated not just medically but with genuine care, dignity, compassion, and respect. The doctors, nursing staff, assistants, and support teams work together like one family to ensure that every patient receives the best possible care.

Thank you once again to Dr. Shardul Lokare, Dr. Shantanu Lokhare, all the RMO doctors, nurses, General Duty Assistants, and the entire Dhanashri Hospital team. Our family will always remain grateful for everything you have done for my mother.

With heartfelt gratitude and respect,

Akash Keny & Family
